content.thinking:
I'm planning the file structure, pulling in builder, math, paint, and texture utilities to construct the creature with glowing golem eyes and other stylistic details.

Now I'm sketching out the golem's anatomy: thick legs with basalt feet, a hunched torso built from frustum shapes with a glowing molten core visible through gaps, a sunken head with glowing eyes, massive arms with rock pauldrons and fists, plus basalt spikes and hexagonal columns along the back and shoulders, all finished with cel-shaded paint and gold accents.

I'm adding gold filigree trims—wrist bands, a belt, and an ornamental chest ring—along with floating ember spheres for a pyro touch instead of glow cards. For the stone material I'm leaning toward a mottled cel paint with explicit lit and shadow tones rather than relying on defaults, keeping the part construction conservative using the existing box, rod, capsule, spike, and frustum helpers.

For the torso, I'm planning a glowing orange core body with separate, slightly larger basalt plates layered on top so the gaps between them reveal the glow underneath without z-fighting. I'm writing a plate helper function that takes position, dimensions, rotation, and paint to generate each box plate.

Now I'm laying out the full figure: feet as boxes, glowing rod legs connecting hip to knee, and shin plates arranged front, side, and back around each leg to build up the armored look.

Still placing body details...

Fists hang low near the floor with gold wrist bands made from torus shapes oriented along the forearm direction. For the head, I'm placing a glowing core inside a stone helm with a brow plate, glowing eyes, a jawbox with a glowing mouth slit and teeth spikes, plus curved basalt horns tipped in gold.

I'm adding a thin gold ring behind the head as a halo and some hanging gold-beaded tassels from the belt for ornamentation. Checking overall proportions, the golem stands about 3.4 meters tall with horns reaching the highest point — I'll skip floating embers and rubble to keep things concise and move on to defining the stone material paint.

Writing paint definitions...

I'm defining a crackStone helper combining lit and shadow paints with a distinct crack color for the shadowed side, then setting up a box helper with typed position, size, and rotation tuples, keeping the type system strict to avoid unused variable errors.

Now I'm mirroring the arm geometry across both sides using a sign factor, placing shoulder, elbow, wrist, and fist joint positions, and building the upper arm as a capsule core with surrounding plates angled to match the arm's lean.

Working out forearm rotation...

I'll use frustumBox sections for the armor plates over limbs, segmenting each limb into multiple pieces with small gaps between them via a lerp-based helper function, and apply the same segmented-plate approach to the torso. Time to write the actual code now.

Working out chest and abdomen plate positions...

Now designing the head: a stone skull box with a darker brow ridge, slanted glowing eye boxes, and a jaw box below that leaves a thin glowing mouth slit between skull and jaw, adjusting the skull's y-position to avoid overlap with the jaw.

Still placing geometry details...

Adding gold caps and a belt with buckle and tassels...

For the hips, I'm splitting the stone plates into two side pieces with a gap so the glow core shows through, letting the buckle hide the seam in front. Then I'm blocking out the feet with a stone base and separate toe plates up front.

Now I'm adding lava-glow accents at the ankle and foot cracks, then building the fist as a stone box with darker knuckle bumps and a glowing seam where it meets the wrist, plus a gold wrist band torus.

For the forearm, I'm orienting the wrist torus along the limb's direction vector, adding tapered forearm plates, an elbow icosahedron with a gold spike, and matching upper arm plates, then sketching the shoulder pauldron with gold trim.

Now I'm adding a tilted gold arc at the base, then planning glowing orange rune glyphs rendered as textured planes on the chest plates and back armor.

I'll add a gold flame emblem resembling a pyro-vision motif on the chest, plus rune texture variants, skip card elements, add small rubble rocks at the feet, and define the export meta object with name, description, style, and commit hash. Writing frustum-based limb plate segments...

Sweep looks good, time to write the final code.
